roleTitle: Predictive Maintenance Engineer, Wind Turbine Fleet Analytics
jobDescription: The wind turbine fleet analytics service predicts component failures for an operator's turbines and raises work orders for the maintenance crews. The Predictive Maintenance Engineer operates the failure models in production: has deployed models into the live scoring service, watches live alert precision against confirmed failures, handles production model incidents such as a sensor feed dropping out, coordinates model releases with the platform team, and documents each model's limitations. The role reports to the head of fleet analytics and works with the platform team, the maintenance planners and the site crews.
requirements: Has deployed failure models into the live scoring service and watches live alert precision against confirmed failures.
Handles production model incidents such as a sensor feed dropping out during the scoring window.
Coordinates model releases with the platform team and records own responsibility boundaries.
Builds and backtests failure models on historical sensor and work-order data under a documented evaluation protocol.
Documents each model's limitations and hand-over conditions in a model card.

evidence.text: Deployed four gearbox and bearing failure models into the live scoring service of the fleet analytics platform over three years, releasing each through the platform team's release pipeline under my own release tickets.

Watched live alert precision against confirmed failures in the weekly review with the maintenance planners, and handled the production model incidents in that period, including two sensor feed drop-outs, with incident records in the platform incident log.
Built and backtested each model on the historical sensor and work-order data under the evaluation protocol agreed with the planners before proposing it for release.
Coordinated model releases with the platform team in the release review, recording in the release ticket which checks were mine and which belonged to the platform team.
Wrote the model card for each model, listing the training data window, the backtest results, the known limitations for turbines without vibration sensors and the hand-over conditions.

Work sample: the release tickets for the four models, the weekly precision review for the last quarter and the incident records for the two sensor feed drop-outs, with the platform incident log identifiers as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: candidate said he 'deployed the failure models to the live scoring service' and 'watched the alerts every week'; asked about incidents, he described the two sensor feed drop-outs and their incident records, which match the resume.

Hiring manager pre-read: the head of fleet analytics wants the packet to show the release tickets and the incident records with dates, and to keep any offline backtesting separate from the live scoring work.
